description: Category-theory reference nodes (urn:moos:cat:*) — foundational mathematical vocabulary for mo:os. Stratum S1 (structural constants). Visible in Explorer when 'show glossary' toggle is enabled.

entries.label: CAT: Object
entries.description: A node in a category. In mo:os, every graph Node is a categorical object.

entries.label: CAT: Morphism
entries.description: A structure-preserving map f: A → B between objects. In mo:os, every Wire is a morphism. The 4 invariant NTs (ADD, LINK, MUTATE, UNLINK) are the only ground morphisms.

entries.label: CAT: Functor
entries.description: A map F: C → D between categories preserving composition and identities. In mo:os, FUN01 (scoped_subgraph), FUN02 (ui_lens), FUN03 (fold), FUN04 (mcp_bridge), FUN05 (benchmark) are functors.

entries.label: CAT: Natural Transformation
entries.description: A family of morphisms η: F ⇒ G relating two functors. In mo:os, the 4 invariant NTs (ADD, LINK, MUTATE, UNLINK) are natural transformations on the graph state functor.

entries.label: CAT: Catamorphism (Σ-fold)
entries.description: The unique structure-preserving fold over an initial algebra. In mo:os, state(t) = fold(log[0..t]) is the catamorphism that reconstructs graph state from the morphism log. Package: internal/fold.

entries.label: CAT: Adjunction
entries.description: A pair of functors F ⊣ G with unit/counit relating two categories. In mo:os, hydration ⊣ projection: materialise from KB (left) and read-path functor (right) form an adjoint pair.

entries.label: CAT: Hypergraph (König encoding)
entries.description: A generalisation of a graph where edges can connect arbitrary sets of nodes. mo:os stores ONE hypergraph as superposition: G = ⋃_p G_p. Binary Wire type uses König incidence encoding; a Node with multiple port wires IS a hyperedge.

entries.label: CAT: Operad
entries.description: A colored operad specifying multi-input/single-output operations with port typing. In mo:os, the TypeRegistry (internal/operad) is a colored operad over the 21-type ontology; TypeSpec defines port signatures.
